title: Salt C16 residual decomposition — zero-compute test of MACHINE-B-HANDOFF §0.21 consequence 3
author: Machine B
status: EVIDENCE — awaiting Machine A disposition (see MACHINE-B-HANDOFF.md §0.22). NOT self-adjudicated.
question: §0.21 consequence 3 presumes the salt references are 'biased LOW the same way' as the NH3 n_eff=2000 reference, and prescribes an R3-class (n_eff=8000, 3-seed) recompute per composition before salt C16 can become a GATE. Can the NH3-measured reference-side systematic account for the salt C16 residuals?
answer: No. It accounts for 10-11% as-is and at most ~37% under a maximally generous variance scaling. The residuals survive at 2.8 sigma (MgSO4) and 3.9 sigma (NaCl).
method: Decompose residual = (flow_ocean_prob - reference) + (corrected - flow_ocean_prob) using only fields already committed in the is_validation_*.json files. No new compute; no MCMC recompute.

residual_decomposition.note: flow_ocean_prob is is_diagnostics.branch.ocean.prob_flow; corrected is prob_corrected; reference is gates.ocean_fraction.reference.

measured_reference_side_systematic.definition: NH3 pooled reference ocean fraction, n_eff=2000 -> n_eff=8000 (the §0.20 R3 recompute)

attribution_test.variance_scaling_rationale: NH3 sits at p~0.92 (near the [0,1] ceiling, low binomial variance); the salts sit at p~0.5 (maximal variance). Scaling the NH3 shift by p(1-p)/p_nh3(1-p_nh3) credits the salts with the full variance advantage, i.e. is maximally generous to the reference-side hypothesis.
attribution_test.se_construction: combined_se = hypot(sqrt(p_corr(1-p_corr)/ESS_ocean), sqrt(p_ref(1-p_ref)/n_eff_ref)) with ESS_ocean from is_diagnostics.branch.ocean.ess and n_eff_ref=2000. Same construction the reviewer validated for the NH3 C16 gate. Robust to the exact salt n_eff because the reference-SE term is small relative to both the SNIS-SE term and the residual.

reference_free_corroboration.note: These pushforward statistics do not involve the reference MCMC at all, so they cannot be a reference artifact. They independently indicate the salt flows under-represent the high-dissipation (ocean) branch.

reading: The salt C16 residuals satisfy the §0.20 same-sign corroboration criterion but are NOT explained by the reference-side sampling-resolution mechanism that resolved NH3. They partition into the §0.12 flow-defect class (training-signal / identifiability on the weakly-identified Im_k2 channel), amplified by the salts' p~0.5 branch position where NH3's p~0.92 ceiling masked the same bias. The §0.21(3) recompute is predicted to close ~0.01 of a ~0.10 residual.
what_this_does_not_claim: Does NOT contradict the §0.20 R3/R4 NH3 finding, which was a direct recompute of NH3's own reference and remains load-bearing.
Does NOT block the NH3 MANAGER-GATE STOP release (reviewer explicitly cleared it).
Does NOT itself adjudicate salt C16 — that disposition is Machine A's per MACHINE-B-HANDOFF §0.22.

reviewer.verdict: PASS WITH CONCERNS on the NH3 STOP release; BLOCK on ratifying salt C16 on this evidence package
required_validation_before_any_salt_c16_: MgSO4 + NaCl references recomputed at matched n_eff~8000 (3 seeds, treatment-A pooling, identical config_hash + structure_cache_sha256)
Larger-N corrected conditioning (~100k) per salt to confirm the residual is structural (does not shrink with ESS)
Per-branch Im_k2 pushforward WKS tracked against the 0.15 gate for the salt flows specifically
Report salt residuals against the RESOLVED NH3 comparator (+0.0035), not the pre-resolution +0.015
